placeOrder calls this.customers.findById(customerId), this.products.findBySku(item.sku), this.products.updateStock(product.sku, product.stock) and this.orders.save(toOrderRecord(draft)), which are persistence reads and writes in a domain file

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit sits in the 'business' layer, which is declared as domain kind. The rubric says a domain file must not carry persistence or I/O, meaning queries or database clients. The exception for constructor parameters as dependency wiring covers application files only. OrderService takes three concrete persistence gateways as constructor parameters: OrderGateway, ProductGateway and CustomerGateway, all from src/persistence (infrastructure). Each method then reads and writes through them: findById, findBySku, updateStock and save. It also converts persistence records to and from domain objects (toOrderRecord, toProduct, toCustomer, toOrder). The class header describes it as a Fowler Service Layer of transaction scripts. That is application or persistence-orchestration work, not a domain role. The domain logic itself (Order.cancel, Product.reserve, PricingPolicy.discountFor, Money) is delegated correctly. The file has no HTTP or framework types, decorators or base classes. The import direction is out of scope and is not counted here. What counts is the persistence I/O the file performs.

violations.message: This domain-layer class performs persistence I/O. It also converts persistence records (toOrderRecord, toOrder, toProduct, toCustomer). That transaction-script and persistence work belongs to the application or infrastructure layer, not the domain.
